transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, the main reason I came in is that I just get pulled off track so easily. Like, I'll be working on something for school, and then I get one message, or I hear a song lyric, or I just get a random idea for something else, and suddenly I've completely lost the thread of what I was supposed to be doing.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're supposed to be sitting still?

Yeah, I do. Um, especially in meetings or, like, portfolio reviews for my classes. I'm almost always bouncing my leg or clicking my pen. I'll be twisting my rings or just shifting around in my chair a lot. I honestly don't really notice I'm doing it until someone looks at me, and then I realize I've been moving the whole time.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Um, no, not really. I don't think so. I mean, I might get sidetracked by things, but I don't usually just act on impulse without thinking about what I'm doing first. That's not really something I've noticed myself struggling with.
Do you have trouble focusing or getting distracted at home, not just in school or during meetings?

No, I haven't really noticed that being an issue at home. It's mostly just when I'm trying to get through schoolwork or sitting in those long reviews. When I'm just hanging out at my apartment, I feel like I do okay.
Have you had trouble with getting pulled off track or feeling restless for as long as you can remember?

Yeah, I think so. Even back in elementary school, um, my teachers used to write comments about me rushing through my worksheets and losing track of directions. They also said I had a habit of talking over my classmates during group work. And my parents actually had to sit right beside me when I did my homework. If they didn't, I would just wander off or start something completely different before I even finished what I was supposed to be doing. So, yeah, it's definitely been happening for as long as I can remember.
Do you often have strong mood swings or get easily upset?
No, I wouldn't say I have strong mood swings or anything like that. I don't really get easily upset, either. My mood is pretty stable most of the time.
Did you run, climb, or play more than other kids when you were little?

Um, not really, no. I mean, I played outside and stuff like any kid, but I don't think I ran or climbed around any more than my friends did. I was pretty average when it came to that kind of physical energy, I think.
Do you have trouble organizing your time or tasks to get everything done?

Um, no, I wouldn't say so. I'm actually pretty okay at keeping my schedule straight. I mean, I have my classes and assignments to keep track of, but I usually know what needs to get done and when. So, organizing my time isn't really something I struggle with.
Do you often find yourself talking more than others in social situations?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I talk to my friends and stuff, but I wouldn't say I talk more than anyone else. I'm probably more of a listener, honestly, or just kind of average. I definitely don't take over conversations or anything like that.
Do you often find it hard to finish tasks or projects because you lose interest or get distracted?

Yeah, I actually do. Like, if a professor gives me a list of revisions for a project, I usually do the first couple right away. But then I kind of... drift into redesigning something else entirely, and I end up leaving one small but really important change completely unfinished. So yeah, I definitely get distracted before finishing the whole thing.
Were you more physically active or restless than your peers when you were a child?

Yeah, I think I was. Like, even back in elementary school, my teachers would write comments about me rushing through worksheets and losing track of directions. They also mentioned that I would talk over my classmates a lot during group work. It was pretty noticeable at home, too. My parents actually had to sit right beside me while I did my homework, because otherwise I would just wander off or start doing something else before I finished. So, yeah, I was definitely pretty restless back then.
Have your difficulties with getting pulled off track, restlessness, or other issues you've mentioned caused you any significant problems in your relationships, work, or other areas of your life?

Yeah, it definitely has. Um, I've actually lost a couple of small freelance contracts because of it, and I even missed out on a portfolio competition recently. It's mostly just because... well, people couldn't really rely on me to follow through cleanly on the details. 

It's pretty frustrating, honestly. It has also made some of my friends and collaborators a bit hesitant to work with me on projects now. Like, they always tell me they really like my ideas, but I think they just don't want to deal with me getting off track when it comes time to actually finish the work.
Have you felt like your difficulties with getting pulled off track and restlessness have caused you significant distress?

Yeah, it really does. I mean, like I was just saying about losing those small freelance contracts and missing out on that portfolio competition... it's pretty upsetting. It bothers me a lot that people feel they can't rely on me to follow through cleanly on things. 

And it definitely causes me a lot of stress knowing that my friends and collaborators are hesitant to work with me now. They always say they like my ideas, but knowing they hold back because they don't trust me to finish the work... yeah, it's really frustrating and definitely gets me down.
Have you experienced difficulties with getting pulled off track or feeling restless in other situations beyond school and work?

Um, I'm not really sure. I mean, I guess it's mostly just been an issue with my freelance stuff and school projects, like I mentioned. I haven't really noticed it being a big problem in other situations, or at least nothing stands out right now.
Have you experienced difficulties with getting pulled off track or feeling restless in social situations with friends or family?

Not really, no. I mean, when I'm just hanging out with friends or family, there's no pressure to finish anything or stick to a schedule, so it doesn't really come up. It's mostly just an issue when I actually have to get work done.
Have you experienced difficulties with getting pulled off track or feeling restless in multiple settings beyond just school and work?
No, I don't think so. Like I said, it really is just school and my freelance projects where I notice it happening. I haven't had issues with it anywhere else.
Did you exhibit any of these behaviors, such as getting pulled off track or feeling restless, before the age of 12?

Yeah, actually. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would write comments on my report cards about me rushing through worksheets or losing track of directions. They also mentioned I had a habit of talking over classmates during group work. And at home, my parents used to have to sit right beside me while I did my homework. If they didn't, I would just wander off or start doing something completely different before I finished what I was supposed to be working on.
Have your difficulties with getting pulled off track or restlessness caused problems in your romantic relationships?

No, I haven't really had any issues with that. I mean, I don't have a boyfriend right now anyway, but even in the past, it's never been a problem in that kind of situation. Like I said, it really only happens when I'm trying to focus on schoolwork or my freelance stuff.
Have you consistently experienced difficulties with getting pulled off track or feeling restless in both school and your freelance work over the past few years?

Yeah, it's been pretty consistent, but it really started causing actual problems about a year and five months ago. That was when I kind of transitioned from doing structured school projects to trying to build my own freelance UX and data-visualization portfolio. Without the set structure, it's just been a lot harder to stay on track.
Have your difficulties with getting pulled off track or restlessness caused any problems in your friendships or made it hard for you to make or keep friends?

Well, it hasn't really stopped me from making friends, but... I guess it has caused some friction when it comes to working with them. Like, some of my friends and people I collaborate with are a bit hesitant to work with me now. They always say they like my ideas, but... I've actually lost a few small freelance contracts, and I even missed out on a portfolio competition, just because people felt they couldn't rely on me to follow through cleanly. So, yeah, it definitely impacts things when other people are depending on me.
